Guar is obtained by grinding the en- dosperms of the seeds of Cyamopsis tetragonolobus. It consists mainly of guar galactomannan. Guar is a white or almost white powder, yielding a mucilage of variable viscosity when dis- solved in water. Practically insoluble in alcohol. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Guar Galactomannan). A yellowish-white powder. It is soluble in cold and hot water; practically insoluble in organic solvents. Its main components are polysaccharides composed of D-galactose and D-mannose at molecular ratios of 1:1.4 to 1:2. The molecules consist of a linear main chain of β-(1→4)-glyco- sidically linked mannopyranoses and single α-(1→6)-glycosidi- cally linked galactopyranoses. USNF 26 (Guar Gum). A gum obtained from the ground en- dosperms of Cyamopsis tetragonolobus (Leguminosae).
